back: Shape, dtype and device (plus whether it requires gradients).
`tensor` copies the NumPy array; `from_numpy` shares its memory.
Records operations in the forward pass and replays them backwards on `.backward()`, adding gradients into the leaves' `.grad`.
Gradients accumulate; three backward calls on $2p$ give `p.grad` = 6, not 2.
`(n_out, n_in)`; computes $xW^\top+b$, the transpose of the NumPy `W`.
Raw logits `(B,K)` and `long` labels `(B,)`; it averages over the batch like the hand-written $(P-Y)/B$.
`eval()` changes layer behaviour (dropout off, batch norm uses running stats); `no_grad()` stops graph recording. Use both for inference.
`shuffle=True` for training only, `drop_last=True` to avoid a short final batch, `num_workers` for background loading.
Move the model once with `model.to(device)` and every batch with `.to(device)`; all operands must share a device.
float16: max 65504, smallest normal $6\times10^{-5}$, needs loss scaling. bfloat16: float32 range, about 3 decimal digits, no scaling needed.
Low-precision forward/backward under `autocast`, float32 master weights; with float16 add `GradScaler`.
`torch.save(model.state_dict(), path)`; rebuild the same architecture, then `load_state_dict(torch.load(path, weights_only=True))`.
Model state, optimiser state, epoch and scheduler state.
`clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm)` after `backward()` and before `step()`; a gradient of norm 5 clipped to 1 is scaled by 1/5.
